title: Chief Martial Law Administrator Regulation 1979 No 49

sections.shortTitle: Chief Martial Law Administrator Regulation 1979 No 49
sections.section: RGLN. - Chief Martial Law Administrator Regulation 1979, No. 49
sections.description:
MARTIAL LAW REGULATIONS
MARTIAL LAW REGULATIONS
By
CHIEF MARTIAL LAW ADMINISTRATOR
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 13th September 1979]
No. 49
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 17th October. 1979]
1. This Regulation shall come
into force on 16th day of October, 1979.
2. The Chief Martial Law
Administrator, or a Martial Law Adminis trator may, if he is of opinion that
the publication or propagation of any matter is prejudicial to Islamic Ideology
or the sovereignty, integrity and security of Pakistan or morality and
maintenance of public order, or the purposes of Martial Law, by order addressed
to a printer, publisher or editor, or to printers, publishers and editors
generally,‑
(a) require that all matters, or
any matter relating to a particular subject or class of subjects, shall, before
being published in any document or class of documents, be submitted for
scrutiny to any authority specified in the order ;
(b) prohibit or regulate the
making or publishing of any document or class of documents, or of any matter
relating to a particular subject or class of subjects or the use of any press.
Explanation.‑In this
Regulation "Press" includes a printing press and all machines,
implements and plant and parts thereof and all materials used for multiplying documents.
3. Whoever contravenes any
provision of this Regulation shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment which
may extend to 10 years and shall also be liable to fine or stripes not
exceeding 25.
4. (1) If any person contravenes
an order made under paragraph 2 then, without prejudice to any other
proceedings which may be taken against such person, the Chief Martial Law
Administrator or the Martial Law Adminis trator concerned may declare to be
forfeited to the Provincial Government every copy of any document published or
made in contravention of such Order and any press used in making of such
document and, if the document so forfeited is a newspaper, the Chief Martial
Law Administrator or the Martial Law Administrator concerned may also cancel
the declaration made and sub scribed in respect of such newspaper under the
Press and Publications Ordinance, 1960 (XV of 1960), or as the case may be,
under the West Pakistan Press and Publications Ordinance, 1963 (West Pakistan
Ordinance No. XXX of 1963);
Explanation.‑"newspaper"
means any daily or periodical work contain ing public news or comments on
public news, and includes such other class of periodical works as the
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette declare to be
newspapers.
(2) Where any document or press
had been declared to be forfeited to the Provincial Government under sub‑paragraph
(1), any police officer or any other official authorised by the Chief Martial
Law Administrator or the Martial Law Administrator concerned in this behalf,
may seize any copy of such document wherever found or such press and may, for
the purpose of such seizure, enter upon and search any premises whereon or
wherein such document or copy thereof is or is reasonably suspected to be, or
such press is situate.
